newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trade near standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trade near standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were near a standstill after brisk sales earlier this week which depleted most showlists in the Texas Panhandle/ western Oklahoma area, feedlot sources said. Kansas feedlots still had cattle left to sell, sources there said.
Bids in Kansas and the Panhandle area at $61.00 to $61.50 per cwt were steady with Wednesday's light sales but were generally passed by owners pricing cattle at $62.00 to $63.00.
Weekly sales in the Panhandle were pegged near 110,000 and in Kansas near 80,000, which was more than some sources had expected earlier in the week.
Active cattle sales suggested packer needs were strong and could be tied to retail fill-in buying following the Independence Day holiday last weekend, market sources said.
Lower boxed beef prices this week and cattle feeders' desire to stay current sparked the sales, albeit at lower prices than last week.
However, a rebound in beef movement Wednesday spurred talk that cattle prices may be near a bottom after dropping $2.00 from last week's top, some sources said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted by USDA off $0.03 to $0.23 per cwt, with 224 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Week-to-date beef movement as of midday totaled 991 loads, compared with 904 load reported sold all of last week. Sales last week were crimped by the holiday on Friday.
